description: Search the NATIONAL BUSINESS REGISTERS by company name and get the register's own id back, a Companies House number, a Norwegian organisasjonsnummer, a Finnish business id, a SIREN, a Japanese corporate number, an Estonian registry code, a CRO number, a CNPJ, a US state entity number, or an LEI. Use this when you want the OFFICIAL REGISTERED ENTITY. Registers searched: Companies House (GB), Enhetsregisteret (NO), PRH/YTJ (FI), Sirene (FR), 法人番号公表サイト (JP), RIK e-Business Register (EE), the Companies Registration Office (IE), the US STATE business registers (one per state the sos-entities pack covers; pass country "US", optionally with a two-letter `state`), and the GLEIF LEI crosswalk, which reaches jurisdictions we have no register pack for (DE, SE, AU, SG...). US EXAMPLE: {name: "IPQualityScore LLC", country: "US", state: "FL"} returns the Florida entity number. A US company is formed in ONE state and may also be registered as a FOREIGN entity in others, so without `state` every covered state register is searched and the several registrations of one company come back as ONE match, which says whether the register it names is the company's own or a foreign registration and names the state it was formed in (Browserbase Inc. is a Delaware corporation found in New York). A state we hold no register for (Delaware, California and most others) is SAID so, and is answered from GLEIF (the state file number GLEIF holds for the company, returned as `gleif_state_registration` and labelled as GLEIF's copy, not a lookup in the state's register) and SEC EDGAR (the registrant's state of incorporation, `sec_state_of_incorporation`), with the counts and what a miss means in `state_coverage.indirect_sources` and the explanation; the covered registers are also searched for foreign registrations of a company formed there. A company with neither an LEI nor an SEC filing is not found, so a miss is never proof it is not a company of that state. With `state`, `match_status: "matched"` means the row is that state's own register or says the company was formed there; a same-name registration in another register that does not say where the company was formed comes back as a candidate with `match_scope: "formation_unstated"` ("other_formation" when it states another place of formation), never as the match, and `registered_elsewhere` counts those registrations as evidence the company exists, none about the state. Without `country`, a name that two jurisdictions both hold exactly is `ambiguous` with both rows listed, never decided by a status or LEI penalty (pass `country` to choose); with `country` US and no `state`, SEC EDGAR is asked too, and a state register that could not answer is named under `unavailable_registers` without voiding an exact-form match. For a state we hold no register for (DE, CA, WY...) the other states' registers are where a foreign registration would be found, so when more than a quarter of them could not answer a no_match comes back `incomplete` (retry) with them listed under `fanout_incomplete` and `unavailable_registers`, never as a clean no_match. For US public companies prefer resolve_entity (CIK + ticker + FIGI). THIS TOOL REFUSES TO GUESS, and that is its point: when two different companies match a name equally well it answers `match_status: "ambiguous"` with BOTH, rather than naming one. A one-word trading name usually IS ambiguous, "Bolt", "Apple", "Next", "Sea", "DNB" each match a well-known group AND unrelated micro-entities whose registered name is exactly that word, so pass `country` when you know it. Every response names EVERY register it asked under `searched[]`, with that register's own as-of date and row count, and a register that could not be reached carries an `error` there rather than reading as zero rows: "we could not ask Companies House" is never the same answer as "this company is not in Britain". `related[]` holds entities that collapsed INTO the match, the same company seen through another register, or another country's arm sharing its LEI, so a multinational returns one answer rather than tying with itself. NOT A PEOPLE SEARCH: sole traders and other natural persons are excluded on the publisher's own legal-form field, never guessed from the shape of a name. resolve_entity shares this matcher and returns these register fields too, but searches the US state registers only through this tool.

country.description: OPTIONAL ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 of the register you mean ("GB", "NO", "FI", "FR", "JP", "EE", "IE", "US", "BR"). Narrows the fan-out, and is frequently the difference between an answer and `ambiguous` on a short name. The Irish register and the US state registers are asked ONLY when you pass "IE" or "US". The GLEIF crosswalk is asked whatever you pass, because for several jurisdictions it is the only register we can name at all.

limit.description: Maximum candidates to return, 1-50 (default 10). Does not change which registers are asked, only how many rivals come back.

name.description: The company name as you have it, in its own script. Pass it VERBATIM, do not strip the legal form ("Oyj", "AS", "株式会社", "Ltd"): in Japanese the form is a PREFIX as often as a suffix and 株式会社花王 and 花王株式会社 are DIFFERENT companies, so the form is often the only evidence that separates two candidates. Diacritics, full-width characters and kana are all handled.

state.description: OPTIONAL two-letter US state ("FL", "NY", "CO"...), with country "US" (implied when country is absent). It means the state where the company is registered or was formed, not where it is headquartered: a Delaware company headquartered in California is "DE", and passing its headquarters state asks a different question (omit `state` if you only know the headquarters). A state we hold a register for narrows the search to that register alone. A state we do not (Delaware, California) is answered from GLEIF and SEC EDGAR, with the coverage stated in `state_coverage`, and every covered register is also searched for foreign registrations of a company formed there. Omit to search every covered state register.
